clue.text: Robert longs to overtake the French racing vehicles

parts.note: Bob is the familiar short form of Robert

indicators.note: the yearning word takes over the French article, wrapping round it here

parts.note: to long is to yearn, which is to sigh, so longs gives sighs
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Some driver called Robert is eager to pass the French competitors in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overtake' here means take over, enclose: the yearning word wraps the article rather than passing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobsleighs are sleds built for speed down an ice run, so they are vehicles made for racing.

clue.text: Indian cricketer lived illicitly with Pakistan's opening trio

indicators.note: acting illicitly suggests something irregular, so these letters are rearranged
the opening trio of a word is its first three letters, here taken from the country's name

explanation.surface: Scandal: a cricketer from India cohabited improperly with the first three members of Pakistan's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening trio' takes PAK, which joins LIVED and 'illicitly' rearranges all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapil Dev was India's all-rounder and captain who lifted the 1983 World Cup, a famous player of that nation.

clue.text: Player at Twickenham the focus of indecent remark

indicators.note: the focus is the central part, so the answer sits in the middle of these two words

explanation.surface: A rugby player is the subject of a rude comment.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is England's national rugby stadium in London; the centre is a rugby back position. The letters run across 'indecent remark'.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union a centre is one of the two backs playing in the middle of the three-quarter line.

clue.text: People initially relish good service

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word relish

parts.note: in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: Customers at first enjoy excellent service in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like the subject of 'relish', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a people, a group sharing descent or ethnicity.

clue.text: A number book into unbelievable game

indicators.note: into says the first pieces go inside the word for unbelievable

parts.note: a tall story is an unbelievable one
a number here is something that numbs, and ether is an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Some figure is booked into an incredible match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'number' as NUMB-er, a thing that numbs: ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetherball is a playground game in which a ball tied to a pole is struck round it.

clue.text: Sport left burden in A&E

indicators.note: in says the burden sits inside the letters of A&E

parts.note: the letters A and E, from the hospital's accident and emergency department
a cross to bear is a burden

explanation.surface: A sports injury leaves a strain on the casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department; here it is just its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Small champion loves large swimming group

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written O, so loves gives two Os

explanation.surface: A little champion adores a big swimming squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a large group of fish moving through the water together.

clue.text: Bill picked up wall game here

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted and so read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a bill is a banknote, a note

explanation.surface: Bill collected a wall game score here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a homophone signal but turns NOTE upward. ETON is the English public school whose own wall game is played there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton wall game is played only at Eton College, so the school is where it happens.

clue.text: Typically taking a very short time

parts.note: someone taking a drug is on it

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the word very loses its tail

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Usually something takes only a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts VERY to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually or as a rule, matching typically.

clue.text: A northerner's course

parts.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's chosen route or path.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse, and course is the usual short word for a racecourse.

clue.text: Coach likes strapping batter's midriff to be bowler's target

indicators.note: strapping means binding round, so the jumble goes round the middle letters
to coach is to train or work over, so these letters are rearranged
the midriff is the middle of the body, so the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket coach enjoys putting a strap round the batsman's waist to give the bowler something to aim at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like the cricket trainer but is the anagram signal, making SKILE; 'midriff' takes the two central letters of 'batter'.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles a bowler rolls a ball to knock down the pins, each pin being a skittle.

clue.text: Talk incessantly about old weapon at sea

indicators.note: about means going round, so the talking phrase surrounds the letter

parts.note: to harp on is to talk about something tediously and repeatedly

explanation.surface: Someone drones on about an antique naval weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpoon is a barbed spear thrown or fired, used at sea to hunt whales.

clue.text: Bear loses right to invest

indicators.note: loses says the letter for right is dropped from the word

parts.note: to bear something is to endure it

explanation.surface: A bear in a market loses the right to put money into a stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' wants its money sense, but here it means endow with a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue someone with a quality is to endow or invest them with it, an old literary verb.

clue.text: Immature flyer is rashly flying after cold

indicators.note: after says the jumbled letters follow the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: flying here means sent scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young insect flies recklessly once the cold sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrysalis is the pupa of a butterfly or moth, the stage before the adult insect can fly.

clue.text: What char does at night for unblemished record?

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, so what she does is clean: she cleans
late means at a late hour, in the night

explanation.surface: A cleaner working the night shift is asked about a spotless history.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charlady, is a British word for a woman paid to clean homes or offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean slate is a record free of past faults, as if a chalk slate had been wiped.

clue.text: Unusually striking way to avoid a commercial overhead?

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual arrangement, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to avoid means to leave out, so the letter a is dropped from the fodder

explanation.surface: A remarkable method of dodging an advert above you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops the A from STRIKING WAY and 'Unusually' rearranges what is left. 'overhead' is a pun: a business cost and something above you.
explanation.definitionFit: Skywriting is advertising traced in smoke by an aircraft, an advert literally in the sky above.

clue.text: Reveal secret to let opposition win

definitions.meaning: to let slip a secret plan
literally to give away a game is to hand victory to the other side

explanation.surface: Letting slip a secret amounts to throwing the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means betraying a secret, and taken literally it means conceding a contest to rivals.

clue.text: Follow round a pair of females in ship's bar

indicators.note: round says the following word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to trail is to follow behind
F is the abbreviation for female, so two give FF

explanation.surface: A man trails two women into the bar on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub but means a rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the handrail round the stern of a ship, a bar in the sense of a rail.

clue.text: Victory banner raised to welcome Hearts player

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the upturned banner takes in the letter
in a down clue raised means lifted up, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a banner is a flag
H is the abbreviation for hearts, the card suit

explanation.surface: Fans raise a victory banner to greet a Hearts footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts, Heart of Midlothian, is an Edinburgh football club, but here H is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing half was a midfield position in old football formations, so a kind of player.

clue.text: Decisive game's influential, if boring

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the word if is put inside

parts.note: a seminal work is a highly influential one

explanation.surface: A crucial match is important, even if dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final decides who goes through to the final, so it is a deciding match.

clue.text: Nearly avoid oddly crude error at the Crucible

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: to miss something is to avoid it

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word crude

explanation.surface: A clumsy mistake at a famous theatre was narrowly avoided.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible is a Sheffield theatre, but it hosts the World Snooker Championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscue is a faulty shot in snooker where the cue slips off the ball.

clue.text: Victor's first to leave ring circling bull

indicators.note: first to leave says the opening letter of the word departs

parts.note: a victor is a winner

explanation.surface: The winner's first act is to leave the bullring with the beast inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is the centre of a target, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target or dartboard the inner is the ring immediately surrounding the bullseye.

clue.text: Some tin got smelted making these?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some molten tin was poured to cast bars.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition: smelted tin is what makes ingots.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingots are blocks of cast metal, the usual product of smelting a metal like tin.

clue.text: Winger, surprisingly sleek, secures try almost

indicators.note: secures means holds fast inside, so the shuffled letters hold the shortened word
surprisingly hints at something unexpected, so these letters are rearranged
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: A rugby wing, remarkably smooth, nearly scores a try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests the rugby player but means a bird: it has wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon, and any bird is a winged creature.

clue.text: Secure measure of speed for flyer

explanation.surface: Fasten a gauge of velocity to a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: Knot means fasten, a nautical unit of speed, and a shorebird, three separate senses.

clue.text: VIP's six at Lord's?

definitions.meaning: a six in cricket is a hit clean over the boundary

explanation.surface: A dignitary hits a six at the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a six is the maximum score from one hit in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A big shot is an important person, and a six is a huge hit in cricket.

clue.text: Small bar at Old Trafford's temporarily free

definitions.meaning: one of the two small crosspieces on top of cricket stumps

explanation.surface: A small pub at the stadium is open for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford here is Lancashire's cricket ground in Manchester, not the football stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bail is a little wooden crosspiece on the stumps; legally, bail releases an accused person pending trial.

clue.text: One helps pupils losing way in Windows

indicators.note: losing says the letters for way are taken off

parts.note: an oculist is an eye doctor, and pupils are parts of the eye
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A teacher who helps pupils gets lost in computer software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests schoolchildren, but they are parts of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculi, plural of oculus, are round windows such as those in domes, from the Latin for eyes.

clue.text: Try phoning Irish town overlooking last event

indicators.note: phoning is talking by voice, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word try, said aloud, gives the prefix spelt tri

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the last letter of the town is missed out

parts.note: Athlone is a town in the middle of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone tries calling an Irish town, ignoring the final competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is a sporting contest combining swimming, cycling and running, an event at the Olympics.
